chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Abu Ali ibn Rashid said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Your mawali have differed, so should I pray behind all of them?' He said: 'Do not pray except behind the one whose religion and trustworthiness you are confident in.'
ai.seo_question: Who should one pray behind when there is disagreement among the mawali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the practical issue of congregational prayer (*Salat al-Jama'ah*) when there is diversity among the *mawali* (freedmen or followers) regarding their religious reliability. He advises praying behind the individual whose *din* (faith) and *amanah* (trustworthiness) are most certain, emphasizing that the validity of the prayer depends on the Imam's religious integrity rather than mere numerical majority or collective presence. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly principle that the Imam of Prayer must be just (*'Adl*) and trustworthy, a key criterion in distinguishing between Sunni and Shia jurisprudence regarding congregational leadership.
